interface.longDescription:
TTMNG Pharmaceutical assist helps pharmacy and herbal-evidence researchers find source-specific facts, inspect original conditions and compare evidence scopes. Read the current project catalog of 243 selected foreign medicine families, 245 exact product contexts and 10,257 medicine records, alongside 170 scientific taxa, 878 herbal clinical records, 168 documentary material scopes and 168 partial constituent profiles containing 691 entries. The service also includes 62 registered research runs with 148 findings, documentary co-use contexts and clearly separated experimental mechanisms.

Select an exact product or scientific name, read the evidence and its citations, and use recorded research before investigating a remaining gap. Evidence retains source dates, plant parts, preparations, measurement units, denominators, calibration, sample counts, negative findings and unresolved limits. Clinical evidence is kept separate from analytical occurrence and mechanistic hypotheses. The backend reads existing evidence; it does not perform new web searches or write new research.

Ordinary users require server-side owner approval. Provisioned OpenAI reviewer accounts have permanent entitlement; normal OAuth token and session lifetimes apply. The service provides reference evidence. It does not diagnose, prescribe, calculate patient-specific doses, predict clinical risk, authenticate a specimen, establish complete chemistry, recommend substitution or certify manufacturing.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.4.0 connects the complete current project evidence snapshot: 243 medicine families, 245 exact product contexts and 10,257 medicine facts; 170 taxa and 878 herbal clinical records; 168 material scopes and 168 partial constituent profiles with 691 entries; 62 research runs with 148 findings; 18 documentary co-use contexts and 13 hypotheses. Seven current-project read tools and three updated Skills replace the unused legacy tools. The existing plugin, Firebase endpoint, OAuth, owner-approved access and permanent reviewer entitlement are retained. No former 1.2.0 corpus is imported. Source conditions, unknowns and clinical/nonclinical distinctions remain explicit.
